summary: Host Alien claimed the MB-003 migration stage. Digital-City claim commit 5e69ebf0e366835547eb3c36e596937fe58565ec pushed to City main with no write conflict. MB-001 migration is COMPLETE and MB-002 migration is held by host Mech, so MB-003 is the lowest-sequence claimable migration. Branch mission/MB-003-worker-gateway created from utopia main c7ef3cd1c6be0155332d03afc3607dfdbf49c205.

Reconnaissance started. Target is the EXISTING building city/02-engineering/02-worker-gateway, which already owns the migrated skill-intake module, so MB-003 must land as a NEW sibling module in that building (skill-intake must not be forked). Donors are DS-Hns @ eeb57ca (worker/task contract, provider adapter, readiness/health) and Codex-Boss @ 8df428e (provider session/router/circuit-breaker/outcome). A third donor clone at the DS-Hns frozen SHA is required before any boundary decision.

Landed three new modules in the EXISTING city/02-engineering/02-worker-gateway building (skill-intake untouched): worker-task-contract (DS-Hns scheduler/lifecycle.js, 23 tests), provider-adapter (Codex-Boss runtimes/runtime.ts + unsupported-runtime.ts + web/provider-runtime-adapter.ts + src/shared/provider-state.ts, 29 tests), provider-resilience (Codex-Boss commander/circuit-breaker.ts + src/shared/provider-outcome.ts, 42 tests). Extended city/CITY_IMPLEMENTATION_MANIFEST.json and the census test; added the mission-incubation provenance contract; documented all of it bilingually in city/docs.

Two real failures. (1) Adding three unbridged modules made the capability registry advertise them to Web and Android as unavailable capabilities, which broke the existing capability-registry and capability-adapters count assertions. (2) My first attempt to consume the migrated breaker called the standalone exported accessors state(breaker,id)/observeFailure(breaker,id); those take a snapshot core, not the object createCircuitBreaker returns, so the bridge threw TypeError on every request. The module's bound methods are the stateful API. A third, self-inflicted failure was caught before commit in the same module family's test expectations.

Repairs. (1) Rather than editing the count assertions, a module-level capabilityProvider flag was added: the three adapter-infrastructure modules declare capabilityProvider:false and the capability registry skips them, so the product capability surface returns to exactly its pre-MB-003 shape and the pre-existing assertions pass untouched. The flag is validated in city/manifest.mjs. (2) The bridge now uses the breaker's bound methods (circuit.state(id), circuit.observeFailure(id)). A new test proves the bridge refuses exactly what the Core refuses, and that a capability-wide EXECUTION_TIMEOUT - a failure, but not a provider-health signal - still must not degrade anything. No assertion was deleted, skipped or weakened.

Full CI-equivalent suite green: pnpm test 59/59, apps/rooms tests 67/67, city/test-all.mjs 224/224, verify-promotion-history.mjs 10 records verified, check:docs SYNCHRONIZED in docs, evidence and data-records. New module tests: worker-task-contract 23, provider-adapter 29, provider-resilience 42 (94 total).

Real consumption verified: services/capability-bridge/bridge.mjs now decides per-capability degradation through the migrated provider-resilience breaker, with Utopia's policy (failureThreshold 1, cooldown 604800000, and only ENGINE_UNAVAILABLE / ADAPTER_UNAVAILABLE counting) supplied as data. tests/capability-bridge.test.mjs drives a real bridge over a real Store: a timeout leaves the capability AVAILABLE, a provider-technical failure degrades it, the Core reaches the same verdict for the same policy, further work is refused with BRIDGE_PENDING, and unrelated capabilities are unaffected. Behaviour is identical to the ad-hoc Set it replaced: a degraded capability is refused before dispatch, so no success is ever observed and nothing ever closes the breaker.

Hosted required CI green for the implementation SHA aff3c283e34b596c6c0ba6c666aed96893b6c395: V0.2 checks run 36570163616 completed success. The claim-stage push 590d041c4398c11f53dce9c821a2c0c44d508edd also ran green under run 36567419904. Local CI-equivalent results on the same tree: pnpm test 59/59, apps/rooms 67/67, city/test-all.mjs 224/224, verify-promotion-history 10 records, check:docs SYNCHRONIZED, Android :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:assembleDebug BUILD SUCCESSFUL (all tasks up-to-date; apps/android unchanged).

MB-003 migration stage complete on host Alien. Three modules landed beside the untouched skill-intake in city/02-engineering/02-worker-gateway: worker-task-contract (DS-Hns), provider-adapter and provider-resilience (Codex-Boss), 94 parity tests. Real consumption: the capability bridge's per-capability degradation decision is owned by the migrated provider-resilience breaker with Utopia's policy supplied as data, exactly equivalent to the ad-hoc Set it replaced. Recorded boundaries, not hidden: two of three modules have no product consumer; circuit-breaker persistence is deferred; DS-Hns's real adapter plane in app/core/plugin-adapters, app/sub-worker and app/engineering was not migrated; and MB-001/MB-003 will conflict at merge time over the manifest, the census test and the bilingual docs. Branch not merged and mission:finalize not run, per the mission-book. City report: Digital-City/mission-book/reports/MB-003/MIGRATION_REPORT.md.

Verification host Mech begins the rule 9 independent review of mission/MB-003-worker-gateway at c5734a5 before reading the Migration Report. Gates on the branch: root 59/59, city 224/224, apps/rooms 67/67. The three migrated modules exist under city/02-engineering/02-worker-gateway (provider-adapter, provider-resilience, worker-task-contract) and the real consumption is the capability bridge delegating its per-capability degradation latch to the migrated circuit breaker.

MB-003 verification is BLOCKED on the Mission's first gate, which requires one real detect-submit-progress-result or unsupported path per host with an installed donor-supported provider and forbids a mock pass. This host has no codex, claude or gemini provider, no pulled Ollama model and no donor-supported local runtime. The migrated provider-adapter wraps caller-supplied hooks and its DONOR.json defers real web-session automation and provider HTTP calls; worker-task-contract defers the real runner spawn seam; services/dev-gateway builds the bridge with no execute hook. A probe confirms unsupportedRuntime refuses honestly and providerRuntimeAdapter only runs a caller hook; a source scan finds no network or spawn seam. Adding a provider client would be new capability, forbidden by rule 10. Other gates green at c5734a5: root 59/59, city 224/224, rooms 67/67. A merge rehearsal found two mechanical conflicts whose reconciliation shape is in the report.

Step 3 opened under response-9-30 R8, which allows an explicit completion repair inside the original MB-003 Mission identity. R8 limits the repair to provider/runner execution, runtime registry/supervisor wiring, spawn/lifecycle, submit/progress/result/evidence, cancel/interruption and donor failure classification from the frozen donors, and states that if no donor-supported real provider environment exists while MB-003 is still valuable, the Mission must remain BLOCKED rather than be masked by a skip.

Step 3 reassessment and provider probe on reconciliation base 168182c47df537f7c6c47d7e42ab3220af40de68 (post-MB-008). Value verdict ROUTE_B_CONTINUE: main declares no provider/runner execution seam and nothing equivalent elsewhere, so SKIPPED_NOT_REQUIRED is not available. Branch was 59 behind / 4 ahead. Probe on host Mech: the donor-supported runtime IS present here, which corrects the earlier BLOCKED finding's environment claim.

Host Mech real donor-backed provider receipt, produced by executing the DONOR'S OWN runner seam unmodified (DS-Hns eeb57ca app/extensions/mega/scheduler/dsh-runner.js) against the runtime it actually spawns: @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.5-rc.1, profile headless, credential route llm-deepseek/deepseek-official via the host's already-authorised key. Receipts: detect and version OK; submit of a bounded read-only job exit 0 returning OK; liveness observable through the donor per-task log; cancel/interrupt via the donor killTree terminated a running job; the migrated unsupportedRuntime refuses with PERMANENT_FAILURE/UNSUPPORTED retryable false; a real provider failure (credential withheld) exited 1 with MISSING_CREDENTIAL and was NOT rewritten as success; the migrated circuit breaker moved CLOSED to OPEN on a provider-technical failure. No secret was printed or logged. This is ONE host's receipt: the Mission gate requires Alien and Mech each, so the gate is NOT met.

MB-003 branch module regression green on the extracted branch tree: skill-intake 22/22, provider-adapter 29/29, provider-resilience 42/42, worker-task-contract 23/23 (116 total, 0 failures). Skill Intake regression, which the Mission requires to stay green, is confirmed green.

Verifier finding, step 3. The earlier BLOCKED reason is CORRECTED on one point but the Mission stays BLOCKED. Correction: this host DOES have a donor-supported real provider path, so 'no provider environment' was wrong for Mech; the earlier probe looked only for provider CLIs on PATH and missed that the donor's own runner targets @deepseek-ai/dsh, installed in the DS-Hns donor app. Mech therefore produced a real receipt. Blocker: the gate requires EACH participating host (Alien and Mech) to leave a real receipt and response-9-30 R7 forbids downgrading to one host. Alien is a different physical host whose working copies do not exist here (COMPUTERNAME MEGA-REP), so Alien's half cannot be produced from this session. No repair was applied and no implementation written: the Mission cannot be finalized or merged without both halves and an unverifiable delta must not sit on an unmerged branch. Blocker retained.

Repair step 3, the missing two-host half, produced by the MIGRATION host on its own physical host. This closes the blocker recorded at 8262a41: the gate requires Migration Host and Verification Host to EACH leave a real donor-supported provider receipt (README section 3 line 90, response-9-30 R8), Mech's half was already recorded, and Alien's half could not be produced from Mech's machine. Alien host MERA-ALIANWARE has D:/DS-Hns at the frozen donor SHA eeb57ca5 with @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.5-rc.1 installed, so the same donor seam app/extensions/mega/scheduler/dsh-runner.js was driven here. Result: ALL EIGHT verdicts true, recorded in .runtime/evidence/mission-book/MB-003/run-3/provider-probe.json.

Alien host real provider receipt, the second half of the two-host gate. Driver: node .runtime/evidence/mission-book/MB-003/run-3/provider-probe.mjs. Eight verdicts, all true: PROVIDER_RUNTIME_PRESENT, REAL_SUBMIT_RESULT, PROGRESS_OBSERVED, CANCEL_INTERRUPT, UNSUPPORTED_REFUSAL, PROVIDER_BREAKER, PROVIDER_ERROR_NOT_REWRITTEN, NO_SECRET_LEAK. @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.5-rc.1 was present and the donor seam's own DSH_BIN resolved to the same binary; a bounded read-only job spawned a real child, the per-task log grew while it lived, and it exited 0 returning the real model answer OK.

Alien receipt, failure and recovery side. The donor's own killTree terminated a different running job (alive before true, alive after false). The migrated unsupportedRuntime refused with PERMANENT_FAILURE, code UNSUPPORTED, retryable false. A deliberately withheld credential produced exit 1 with MISSING_CREDENTIAL and was NOT rewritten as success. The migrated circuit breaker went CLOSED to OPEN, refused admission while open, and reached HALF_OPEN after cooldown. The host's already-authorised credential was passed to the child process only and appears in no job log, no record and no console output.

CHANGE_APPLIED — the deferred donor execution seam is now migrated. New City module city/02-engineering/02-worker-gateway/worker-runner ports DS-Hns app/extensions/mega/scheduler/dsh-runner.js (frozen eeb57ca5) as plain ESM: createRunner(seams) exposes startJob, killTree, childEnv, dshBin and nodeExecutable. The donor's only two outside dependencies (require of ../utils/paths giving PATHS/ROOT, and ../utils/workspace giving getWorkspaceRoot) became injected host seams, so the module owns no drive letter. Behaviour is otherwise line-for-line: the same seven pinned childEnv keys in the same order with the same defaults and overrides spread last, the same argv, cwd, stdio triple and windowsHide, the same append log tee with child.logStream, the same return shape, and the same taskkill.exe PID/T/F call with the donor's empty catch. Registered in the manifest and the census with capabilityProvider false. scheduler.js, gate.js and system.js stay deferred and are recorded in DONOR.json.

RUNTIME_PASS — the engineering-book real execution gate, driven through the PORTED seam rather than the donor file. Driver .runtime/evidence/mission-book/MB-003/run-4/ported-seam-gate.mjs. Five verdicts, all true: the ported dshBin resolved @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.1.5-rc.1; a bounded read-only job started by the ported startJob spawned a real child (pid 59024), its tee log grew while it lived, and it exited 0 with the real model answer OK and no key material; the ported killTree terminated a different running job (alive before true, after false); the migrated unsupportedRuntime refused with PERMANENT_FAILURE/UNSUPPORTED/retryable false; the migrated circuit breaker went CLOSED to OPEN and refused admission. The default log path was also derived from the task id exactly as the donor did.

TEST_PASS — module and tree regressions after registering worker-runner. worker-runner 15/15 (injected fake spawn/fs, no real process). Skill Intake 22/22, provider-adapter 29/29, provider-resilience 42/42, worker-task-contract 23/23. City suite 239/239, root suite 59/59, rooms 67/67, census 7/7.
